name: Kinetic Typography
visualIdentity: Explicitly named text-led motion design. Size, weight, spacing, position, and movement order carry the narrative. Use concise copy, clear holds, consistent alignment, and readable continuity.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: quotes, manifestos, copy-led spots, lyric videos, rhythmic promos, spoken word, corporate statements, conference openers, and data-light announcements. It can support product or editorial storytelling. These are suitability judgments from the source, not guarantees.
limitations: Use motion only when it helps explain the subject. Preserve reading time and hierarchy; avoid uniform spring motion on every letter. Optional scrambled reveals suit short titles and must retain exact, accessible final copy. Omit pinned or chapter patterns when they obscure meaning, crop key details, disrupt layout, or violate continuous-shot or loop needs.
palette: For new artwork without approved colors, suggested roles are cream background #FAF5E9, ink foreground #252D39, and warm red accent #B84F3F. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Exact task, brand, source, and semantic colors take precedence; preserve roles and asset colors. Use discrete tokens, no proposed gradient, and recheck contrast on actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Animate measured words or glyph groups through deliberate layout changes; convert text to verified paths only for needed deformation. Preserve holds and authored cuts, impacts, or constant-speed motion. Video state must be deterministic and seekable from composition time. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to pinned-stage recomposition, chapter handoffs, or story states, with stable release and reversible progress; provide keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior as applicable.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience, honoring supplied audio requirements. If beat-mapped, analyze the actual track, land key words on beats, and keep phrase holds readable. Synchronize and mix through the render pipeline; check intelligibility, clipping, balance, and sync.
assetRequirements: Load and measure actual fonts; group real text or prepared glyphs, preserving exact copy and readable accessible text. Use approved assets and palettes as supplied. Optional diagrams can be exported as layered SVG or raster; flattened artwork will not remain separately editable. Preload assets and fonts, seed random values, and bake or deterministically evaluate stateful motion.
combinations: Stands alone for quotes, manifestos, and copy-led spots. With beat mapping, words follow analyzed music while retaining phrase holds and reserving accent for stressed words. With a Swiss grid, text travels on horizontal or vertical axes and settles to shared baselines; keep the grid fixed and use cream, ink, and red. Avoid unrelated photography or drifting motion that breaks the grid.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS and SVG own typography, layout, paths, and masks; a selected motion engine owns trajectories and easing, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only for verified HyperFrames unavailability or limitation, with the reason recorded. Keep visuals and motion style-specific. Interactive scroll is not a video dependency; inspect representative frames, seeks, and final playback.
